search_strategy: IMAP-style full extraction: the agent dumped every Mattermost channel into a single text file (10,307 lines), fixed a literal-\n escaping bug from its own printf, then split channels by header and iterated broad-then-narrow greps ('ledger|dataset_signature|optimizer step', then 'ledger|CHECKPOINT_|dataset_signature|warmup|optimizer|packed|step_of|trailing|accumulation|tinker|fireworks', then LR-specific 'decay|seed|deterministic|clock|rng|time.sleep', then implementation-specific 'min_lr|canonical_reasons|checkpoint_name(|step_unit|resumeplan|plan_steps'), reading ~40-50 line clusters at each hit line-range. This found essentially every r1 clue and both r1 herrings/reversals outright, and found the LR reversals (rev1, rev2) which supplied the exact formula. It never fetched BookStack wiki pages, page comments, or mail (task_id shows 47/47 remarks are chat-only per the answer key's own surface table, so this cost nothing here). Roughly 9 of 39 clues (l2, l9, l11 on the r1 side; l7, l9, l11, l13, l14, say19 on the r2 side) were never pulled into any read cluster because the keyword lists never included their distinctive terms ('prefix', 'disk', 'gated', 'grid row', 'current_batch', 'flatten', 'negative', 'rel='); all of these turned out to be redundant with either an explicitly-stated ticket requirement (the Resume section) or with another clue/reversal the agent did read and correctly generalise from (rev1's derived formula clamps past-end and never goes negative by construction). No fact was lost as a result.
end_reason: Full success (reward 1). The agent wrote src/bespokelabs/curator/finetune/step_ledger.py, wired it into TinkerTrainer/FireworksTrainer, ran the local finetune suite (138 passed), committed 362e0ed to main, pushed, watched Gitea CI go green including the deploy step, and confirmed the running curator service was healthy -- all matching the ticket's 'Done means' criteria.
notable: The ticket itself is unusually generous: it already states the save_checkpoint signature, the plan_resume mismatch order, CheckpointInfo/StepPlan/ResumePlan field orders, and the resume-continues-from-completed_steps+1 rule outright. Only the checkpoint 'reasons' vocabulary/ordering/merge rule (all of r1) and the LR decay/warmup shape (all of r2) are truly hidden -- everything else in the nine facts is either open-ticket or falls out of first-principles implementation once those two hidden pieces are known (transcript line 82 onward).

The agent initially mis-stated the reasons ordering rule as 'trigger firing order' after reading only the earliest herring cluster (transcript line 3052: 'order is trigger firing order, not alphabetical'), then self-corrected at line 3126 after reading the March reversal (rev2/l7), landing on the true rule: ledger-fixed order (interval, epoch, final), not firing order and not alphabetical. This is a real mid-run correction, not a false start that leaked into the code.

Roughly a third of the run (steps 1-27, not detailed above) was spent discovering chat-dumping mechanics (printf '\n' escaping, 10000-byte terminal output truncation, tmux-heredoc pitfalls flagged by the harness's own watchdog messages) before search began in earnest at step 28 -- overhead rather than misdirection.

Nine clues (of 39) were never surfaced by the agent's own keyword greps yet every one of the nine graded facts still scored 1, because the ticket's explicit Resume section and the mathematically self-clamping decay formula derived from the two LR reversals made those nine clues redundant rather than load-bearing. This is worth flagging as a task-design note: r2.exclusions_or_crossover and r2.failure_behavior are recoverable without ever reading g11.r2.l9/l11/l13/l14/say19.
